data.name: Clayton
data.gender_notes: Clayton is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Old English 'clet' meaning 'clay'. The name Clayton originally meant 'settlement, clearing' and was popular in Anglo-Saxon England. It was later adopted as a surname by the Normans and passed down through generations. The name Clayton carries the meaning “Settlement, Clearing” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Clayton usually hope their child will grow to embody settlement, clearing and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name Clayton may symbolize the idea of creation or new beginnings. It can also be seen as a reminder of the importance of remaining grounded and connected to the earth, as clay is a natural and essential element.

in_greek.name: Κλέιτον
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο όρος Κλέιτον προέρχεται από την αγγλική γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'πεδίο από πηλό' ή 'τόπος πήλινος'. In Christian tradition, names with such origins often symbolize a connection to the earth or specific natural resources. Clayton, as a given name, may signify a person with roots in such a place or someone associated with the qualities of clay, such as humility and malleability.
